tool_input.content:
test(mission): prove the MCP guard is wired, pin the empty-item case

Review round on PR #517. Two findings, one real.

The MCP create handler is the only place the contract truncation guard
is wired by hand — results, reflections, and corrections carry it
inside their strict decoder, but DecodeContractStrict deliberately does
not, because it also reads contracts back off disk. Nothing under
internal/mcp exercised it, so deleting the call left every
internal/mission and cmd/ethos test green while handleMission
(method: create) persisted a contract whose criterion had been
shortened to "PR". A guard nothing proves is wired is this cluster's
defect class.

Falsified by deleting the call: internal/mcp FAILs on
TestHandleMission_CreateRefusesHashTruncatedCriterion with 'create
accepted a criterion cut short at an unquoted #', and every other
package stays green. The two CLI call sites were checked the same way
and already have equivalent coverage — deleting mission.go:1094 fails
TestMissionCreate_RefusesHashTruncatedCriterion, deleting :2374 fails
TestMissionLint_RefusesHashTruncatedCriterion. All three mutations
reverted.

Also pins the empty-sequence-item case that two reviewers have now
independently suspected. It does not reproduce, and the reason is not
the one either proposed: a valueless item does not hang its comment on
the null value node, yaml.v3 moves it to the HeadComment of the NEXT
item, and hashTruncated reads LineComment only. Probe output is in the
test comment so the next reviewer gets an answer from the test.

That also corrects my own round-2 report, which said the comment
'landed on the key every time'. True for mappings, wrong for
sequences, where there is no key. The conclusion held; the description
of why did not.

Tests only. No behaviour change, so no CHANGELOG entry.

29 ok, 0 FAIL with -race.
